FOOTPRINT · LEGAL & YOUR DATA

Privacy policy

Last updated October 22, 2026

This Privacy Notice explains how Footprint ("we," "us," or "our") accesses, collects, stores, uses, and shares personal information when you use our Services. This includes downloading and using the Footprint mobile application or another application that links to this notice, and interacting with us through related marketing or events.

Questions or concerns? This notice describes your privacy rights and choices. Footprint is responsible for decisions about the processing of your personal information. If you disagree with our policies and practices, please do not use the Services. For questions, email amp10432@nyu.edu.

Summary of key points

Use the links below or the table of contents to explore the notice.

  • Information we process. The information involved depends on how you use our Services, the choices you make, and the features you use. See information we collect.
  • Sensitive information. We may process sensitive information, including health data, where needed with your consent or as otherwise allowed by law. See sensitive information.
  • Third-party collection. We do not collect information from third parties. See also the description of optional social logins.
  • Use of information. We use information to operate, improve, and administer the Services; communicate with you; protect security; prevent fraud; and meet legal obligations. Other uses may require consent. See processing purposes.
  • Sharing. Information may be shared in the circumstances described under when and with whom we share information.
  • Security. Organizational and technical safeguards help protect information, but no transmission or storage system offers guaranteed security. See security measures.
  • Your rights. Available rights depend on your location and applicable law. See privacy rights and how to make a request.

1. What information do we collect?

Information you provide

We collect information you voluntarily provide when registering, requesting information about our products, participating in the Services, or contacting us. Depending on your interactions and choices, this may include:

  • Names, phone numbers, email addresses, and usernames
  • Passwords and other contact or authentication data
  • Contact preferences
  • Billing addresses and debit or credit card numbers

Sensitive information

We process health data when necessary with your consent or where otherwise permitted by applicable law.

Social media login information

If you choose to register through an existing social media account, such as Facebook or X, we may receive profile information from that provider. See section 8.

Application data

When using the application, information collected may include:

  • Geolocation. With device permission, location may be tracked continuously or while you use the app to provide location-based features. You can change permissions in device settings.
  • Device access. We may request access to features including the camera, microphone, reminders, social media accounts, or other device functions. Permissions can be changed in device settings.
  • Device information. We automatically collect details such as device identifiers, model and manufacturer, operating system and version, configuration, application identifiers, browser information, carrier or internet provider, IP address, network information, and features accessed.

This information supports app operation, security, troubleshooting, and internal analytics and reporting. Information you provide should be accurate, complete, and kept up to date.

2. How do we process your information?

We process information to provide, improve, and administer our Services, communicate with you, maintain security, prevent fraud, and comply with law. Uses also depend on how you interact with us, including:

  • Account management. Creating and authenticating accounts, enabling sign-in, and keeping accounts operational.
  • Targeted advertising. Developing and displaying personalized content and advertising based on interests, location, and other information.
  • Vital interests. Protecting an individual's vital interests, including preventing harm where necessary.

Other processing purposes may require your prior explicit consent.

3. What legal bases do we rely on to process your information?

We process personal information when we believe a valid basis under applicable law allows it, including consent, legal obligations, providing services or meeting contractual commitments, protecting rights, or legitimate business interests.

European Union and United Kingdom

  • Consent. Permission for a specific purpose, which you may withdraw.
  • Legitimate interests. Processing reasonably needed for business interests that do not outweigh your interests and fundamental rights, such as developing relevant advertising.
  • Legal obligations. Meeting legal duties, cooperating with regulators or law enforcement, defending legal rights, or providing evidence in litigation.
  • Vital interests. Addressing circumstances involving possible threats to someone's safety.

Canada

We may rely on express or implied consent where applicable, and you may withdraw it. In exceptional circumstances, applicable law may permit processing without consent. These circumstances may include:

  • Urgent collection in an individual's interests when consent cannot be obtained promptly
  • Investigations, fraud prevention, and detecting fraud
  • Business transactions subject to applicable conditions
  • Information in a witness statement needed for an insurance claim
  • Identifying injured, ill, or deceased people and contacting next of kin
  • Reasonable grounds to suspect financial abuse
  • Investigating an agreement breach or violation of Canadian or provincial law where consent would undermine information accuracy or availability
  • Compliance with subpoenas, warrants, court orders, or court production rules
  • Professional or employment information used consistently with the purpose for which it was produced
  • Collection solely for journalistic, artistic, or literary purposes
  • Public information specified by regulation
  • Disclosure of de-identified information for approved research or statistics with ethics oversight and confidentiality commitments

4. When and with whom do we share your personal information?

We may share or transfer information in connection with a merger, asset sale, financing, acquisition, or negotiations about those transactions.

Google Maps Platform APIs. Information may be shared with Google Maps Platform services, including Maps and Places APIs. GPS, Wi-Fi, and cellular signals may help estimate location, and accuracy can vary with conditions. We obtain and cache location on your device. You may revoke consent by contacting us using the contact details below.

5. What is our stance on third-party websites?

The Services may link to external websites, online services, or mobile applications, or display advertisements from unaffiliated third parties. A link does not mean we endorse the third party. Their content, privacy practices, and security are outside our control, and this notice does not cover information they collect. We make no guarantee about those services or the safety of information you share with them. Review their policies and contact them directly with questions.

6. Do we use cookies and other tracking technologies?

We may use cookies, web beacons, pixels, and similar technologies to collect and store information, secure accounts and Services, prevent crashes, fix errors, remember preferences, and support basic functions.

We also permit third-party analytics and advertising technologies, including interest-based advertising on our Services and other websites. Where this processing counts as a sale, sharing, or targeted advertising under applicable US state laws, you may request to opt out as described in section 13.

For the current landing page's specific technology disclosures, see the Cookie policy.

7. Do we offer artificial intelligence-based products?

Our Services include features or tools powered by artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies ("AI Products"). These include AI applications, predictive analytics, and machine learning models.

Personal information used by these products is processed under this notice and our agreements with third parties, with safeguards for the information throughout that processing.

8. How do we handle your social logins?

If you register or sign in using a third-party social media account, we receive profile information from that provider. Depending on the provider, this may include your name, email address, friends list, profile picture, and information you make public.

We use this information for purposes described in this notice or explained within the Services. The provider's separate use of your information is outside our control. Review its privacy notice and settings to understand its collection, use, and sharing.

9. How long do we keep your information?

We retain personal information as needed for the purposes described here, unless law requires or permits longer retention, including for tax or accounting obligations. Apart from those requirements, the notice does not identify a purpose that requires keeping information beyond the time you maintain an account.

When a legitimate ongoing business need ends, we delete or anonymize information. If immediate deletion is not possible, including in backup archives, we securely store and isolate it from further processing until deletion becomes possible.

10. How do we keep your information safe?

We use reasonable technical and organizational safeguards intended to protect personal information. No internet transmission or storage technology is completely secure, and safeguards cannot guarantee that unauthorized parties will never access, collect, modify, or steal information. Use the Services in a secure environment; transmission to and from them carries risk.

11. What are your privacy rights?

Your rights depend on your US state or country, province, or region of residence, including the EEA, UK, Switzerland, and Canada. Available rights may include access and a copy of information, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, objection to processing, and protections concerning automated decision-making.

If a solely automated decision has legal or similarly significant effects, we will inform you, explain the main factors, and offer a way to request human review. Contact us to make a request; requests are considered under applicable data protection law.

Complaints

UK users may complain directly to amp10432@nyu.edu or by post using our address. We will acknowledge complaints within 30 days, investigate without unjustifiable delay, and explain progress and the outcome.

If unsatisfied, you may contact the UK's Information Commissioner's Office: ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint; telephone 0303 123 1113; or write to Information Commissioner's Office, Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire, SK9 5AF. EEA residents may contact their Member State data protection authority; Swiss residents may contact the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

Withdrawing your consent

You may withdraw consent by contacting us or updating preferences. Withdrawal does not change the lawfulness of earlier processing or processing permitted on another lawful basis.

Account information

You can review or update your account through account settings. On a request to terminate, we deactivate or delete your account and information from active databases. Some information may be kept to prevent fraud, troubleshoot issues, support investigations, enforce terms, or meet legal requirements.

Cookies and similar technologies

Most browsers let you remove or reject cookies. Doing so may affect features. You may also exercise applicable advertising opt-out rights. Questions about your rights can be sent to amp10432@nyu.edu.

12. Controls for Do-Not-Track features

Browsers and some mobile systems offer Do-Not-Track (DNT) settings to signal a preference against online tracking. The Services do not currently respond to DNT browser signals. If a standard the Services must follow is adopted, this notice will be revised to explain the practice.

13. Do United States residents have specific privacy rights?

Depending on applicable state law, residents of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Oregon, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, or Virginia may have rights to access, correct, obtain a copy of, or delete information, and withdraw consent. Rights may be subject to exceptions.

We collect sensitive information for purposes allowed by law or with consent. It may be used or disclosed to service providers or contractors for specified purposes. You may have a right to limit this use or disclosure. We do not use sensitive information to infer characteristics about you.

Other personal information may be collected during support interactions, surveys, contests, and providing Services or answering inquiries.

Your rights

  • Know whether personal information is processed, access it, correct inaccuracies, request deletion, and obtain a copy
  • Exercise rights without discrimination
  • Opt out of targeted advertising, sale, or profiling for decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
  • Where applicable, receive categories of data processed, categories of recipients, or a list of specific third parties receiving data
  • Where applicable, review, question, or correct profiling; limit sensitive-information use; or opt out of certain sensitive-data collection or voice and facial recognition processing

Requests and verification

To exercise rights, email michaelshih2007@gmail.com or use the contact details below. An authorized agent may submit a request with valid proof of authority. We verify identity or authority using request information; additional information may be needed when existing records are insufficient. Agent requests may require your written and signed permission.

Appeals

If a request is declined, you may appeal by emailing amp10432@nyu.edu. We will provide a written response explaining action taken and the reasons. If an appeal is denied, you may complain to your state attorney general.

California "Shine The Light" requests

California residents may submit an annual, free written request for information about categories of personal information disclosed to third parties for direct marketing in the prior calendar year, and those parties' names and addresses. Send requests using our contact details.

14. Do we make updates to this notice?

We may revise this notice and change the date at the top. Material changes may be announced prominently or through a direct notification. Review the notice periodically for updated information.

16. How can you review, update, or delete the data we collect from you?

Depending on applicable law, you may request access to information, details of processing, corrections, deletion, or withdrawal of consent, subject to legal limits.

Submit a data subject access request by email. Include the type of request and the email associated with your account. Do not send your password. This website does not submit or process requests directly.
